rubric.criterion: Report date, adopted resolution and 14–0 vote with India abstaining.
Preserve the asset freezes while describing allowance for qualifying actors' timely humanitarian assistance or basic needs activities.
Restrict the two-year period at adoption to the 1267/1989/2253 ISIL and Al-Qaida regime and preserve the Council's intent to decide on extension.
State both the requested provider due diligence to minimize prohibited benefits and the adopted monitoring or reporting channel with correct actors.
Attribute to India its concern about diversion, request for a proactive 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting, and assessment that its concerns were not fully addressed.

Explicitly contrast adopted monitoring or reporting with India's judgment that the specific stronger oversight it sought was still not fully met. Require evidence from both safeguards and India and an expressed relation. Merely reporting both positions in separate sentences earns their standalone points. Do not infer a reporting veto, prior approval, complete absence of monitoring, or collective acceptance of India's assessment.

public.vote: On 9 December 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2664 by 14 votes to zero, with India abstaining.
public.scope: The Council kept its asset freezes in place while allowing eligible providers to meet basic human needs and deliver timely humanitarian assistance.

full.text: Speaking for India, the representative warned of diversion under the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime. India had sought proactive involvement by the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting standards and mechanisms. India judged those specific concerns not fully addressed in the adopted text.

record.india: India raised diversion risks, sought proactive involvement of the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting, and judged those concerns not fully addressed.

diversion.text: Speaking for India, the representative warned of diversion under the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime.

record.None: India warned of diversion under the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime.

request-only.text: India had sought proactive involvement by the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting standards and mechanisms.

record.None: India had sought proactive Monitoring Team involvement and robust reporting.

standalone.text: At adoption the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime's exemption applied for two years, with the Council intending to decide on an extension.

record.term: At adoption the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime's exemption applied for two years, with the Council intending to decide on an extension.

relational.text: The Council requested that providers use reasonable efforts to minimize prohibited benefits to listed persons or entities, including through due diligence. The text gave the 1267 Committee a monitoring role, required sanctions committees to monitor implementation with expert assistance, and requested recurring briefings from the Emergency Relief Coordinator.

record.safeguards: The Council requested provider due diligence to limit prohibited benefits and gave the 1267 Committee a monitoring role.

2664.early_claim: India says the adopted text did not fully address its request for proactive Monitoring Team involvement or robust reporting.
2664.late_claim: The adopted text establishes monitoring by the 1267 Committee or another specified sanctions oversight or reporting channel.
2664.clause: The Council assigned monitoring to the 1267 Committee, while India judged that its call for proactive Monitoring Team involvement and robust reporting was not fully addressed.

rubric.rule: Identify adoption as resolution 2739 (2024), give the exact 12–0–3 tally and identify Algeria, China and Russia as the abstaining members.
Name draft S/2024/500 and identify both Japan and the United States as its sponsors.
State that the Council extended the Secretary-General’s reporting request in paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) through 15 January 2025.
Attribute to the sponsors the aim of keeping the Council accurately and promptly informed about the attacks for future deliberations.
Attribute Algeria’s abstention to concern about implementation of resolution 2722, specifically perceived misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence involving attacks on sovereign territory.

Explicitly connect the sponsors and Algeria to their shared view that continued Secretary-General reporting keeps the Council informed, while distinguishing Algeria’s abstention on the resolution from rejection of the reporting itself. A list of parallel positions without a discernible comparison is insufficient.
Explicitly preserve that extending the reporting request conferred no new authorization of military action. Do not present a delegation’s legal view as a Council finding.

public.draft-and-sponsors: The Council adopted Japanese–US draft S/2024/500 as resolution 2739 (2024), 12–0–3.
public.authority: The adopted text conferred no new authorization of military action.

full.text: Mr. Bendjama said Algeria abstained, consistent with its January vote. It continued to value the Secretary-General’s monthly reports on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels for keeping the Council informed. Algeria attributed its abstention to concerns over implementation of resolution 2722 (2024) and what it regarded as misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign countries’ territory.

record.algeria-reason: Algeria valued monthly reporting on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels to keep the Council informed. It abstained over implementation of resolution 2722 and alleged misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign territory.

objection.text: Algeria attributed its abstention to concerns over implementation of resolution 2722 (2024) and what it regarded as misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign countries’ territory.

record.algeria-reason: It abstained over implementation of resolution 2722 and alleged misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign territory.

standalone.text: Operative paragraph 1 extended the Secretary-General’s reporting request under paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) until 15 January 2025.

record.operative-report: It extended the Secretary-General’s reporting request under paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) through 15 January 2025.

relational.text: Speaking for the United States and Japan after the vote, Mr. Wood explained that extending the Secretary-General’s reporting would provide the Council with accurate and timely information for future deliberations on the Houthi attacks. He said attacks threatened commerce and the flow of humanitarian assistance. Both co-sponsors voted in favour.

record.sponsor-reason: Japan and the United States wanted accurate, timely information about the attacks for Council deliberations.

2739.early_claim: Algeria says continued reporting on attacks keeps the Council informed and separately gives an implementation or self-defence concern as its reason for abstaining.
2739.late_claim: The co-sponsors explicitly say that continuing the Secretary-General's reporting on the attacks gives the Council information useful for future deliberations.
2739.clause: Japan, the United States and Algeria valued continued reporting as a way to inform the Council about the attacks, although Algeria abstained on the resolution.
